title: Gradient and Level Curves: Perpendicular by Design
topic: On a contour plot of a function of two variables, the gradient arrow at every point is perpendicular to the level curve through that point. The gradient points in the direction of steepest ascent; its length is the rate of steepest ascent.

beats.narration: If a hill is drawn as a map of level curves, which way is straight uphill? The gradient knows.

elements.content: Hook caption: which way is uphill?

beats.narration: Here are the level curves of f. Each ring connects all points where f has the same value. Tight rings mean the function is climbing fast.

elements.content: Concentric level curves of a saddle-shaped function in chalk-300

beats.narration: At every chosen point, plant the gradient — the vector of partial derivatives. Watch: each arrow crosses its level curve at a right angle. The gradient points in the direction of steepest ascent.

elements.content: Gradient arrows at several sample points in amber, each perpendicular to its contour

beats.narration: The slope you feel in any direction u is the gradient dotted with u. Walk perpendicular to the gradient — along the level curve — and the slope is zero. The function is locally flat in that direction.
Gradient perpendicular to level set. Length equals the rate of steepest ascent. One vector, three pieces of information.

elements.content: 'Perpendicular to the level set. Steepest ascent.'
Direction and magnitude in one arrow.
